🏃‍♂️ Are Palantir and other big tech rats fleeing Trump’s ship as midterms threaten his power?
👉 US tech companies closely aligned with Donald Trump are reportedly wooing his political opponents ahead of the November midterm elections.
Meta, Palantir and other companies reportedly fear that a possible Democratic takeover of the US Congress could put their financial ties to Trump under scrutiny, exposing them to subpoenas and congressional hearings, according to The Wall Street Journal. Democrats need just four seats in the Senate and three in the House to take control of Congress.
So, to avoid potential investigations, executives are donating heavily to Democrats, hiring former Democratic aides and setting up teams to assess their vulnerabilities.
🔴 The move by exchange & prediction traders Kalshi - which has hired Democrat aides - is especially telling, given that it hired Donald Trump Jr. as its strategic advisor in January 2025. In March, Trump Jr. fought to shield the rapidly expanding industry from scrutiny by state and federal regulators – while rumors of insider [trading swirl around the Trump family](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73669). Is Kalshi about to turn its back on him?
🔴 At Meta, Palantir, Amazon and Chevron, executives are reportedly preparing for potential congressional probes and hearings
🔴 Meta has donated at least $10 million to nonprofit groups aligned with Democratic House and Senate leaders – but it is also hedging its bets with another $10 million to similar groups supporting Republican candidates
🔴 Palantir’s position is less straightforward. In April, The Hill reported that Democrats were rejecting the company’s donations, wary of its growing political toxicity over links to mass civilian deaths in Gaza and immigration raids in the US. Palantir has secured several major deals under Trump’s second term, including a $30 million ICE contract for an “Immigration Lifestyle Operating System”, a $1 billion DHS purchasing agreement, and a $10 billion ten-year [contract with the Pentagon](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73414)
Probes underway
Donald Trump Jr. and Trump's son-in-law [Jared Kushner](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73148) are already under scrutiny:
➡️ In August, US lawmakers opened a probe into 1789 Capital, the venture firm where Trump Jr. sits on the board, questioning its lucrative investments in companies that secured government contracts
➡️ Earlier this year, lawmakers also began scrutinizing Kushner’s overseas business dealings while he participates in US peace efforts
➡️ If Democrats win, they could use subpoena power to compel Trump family members to testify about their controversial financial dealings
Perhaps if Trump had not pursued aggressive immigration crackdowns, pressured Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu to secure peace in Gaza, or launched the humiliating war in Iran, he might have had better odds of holding onto power. Even his efforts to stave off a US financial crisis with [Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73674) and [AI giants'](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73683) maneuvers may not be enough to save him.

events.text:
🇮🇷📌 Gibraltar: Iran may have hidden leverage over another key strait to choke NATO economies
Iran has demonstrated its powerful leverage over the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. But could it reach more strategic waterways?
Perhaps many have forgotten, but in December 2023, Brigadier General Mohammad Reza Naqdi, a senior Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) commander, warned that the US and its allies could face the closure of the Mediterranean Sea, the Strait of Gibraltar and other strategic waterways in response to their support for Israel’s war in Gaza. He did not elaborate on how.
Naqdi’s statement grabbed headlines, but many at the time questioned Iran’s ability to project power as far as Gibraltar.
The Strait of Gibraltar
It is the Atlantic Ocean’s only door into the Mediterranean while separating Europe from Africa. Roughly 58 km long and just 14 km wide at its narrowest point, it lies between southern Spain and Morocco, with the British territory of Gibraltar and[ the Spanish exclave of Ceuta along its shores](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72928).
👉 It is one of the world’s most stable chokepoints with about 100,000–110,000 vessels passing through each year, roughly 300 a day. It sees around 10% of global seaborne trade worth $1.1 trillion and around 3.3 million barrels/day of oil go through it.
A potential blockade of the Strait of Gibraltar could choke the maritime gateway to the Mediterranean, disrupting commercial shipping, energy supplies and NATO naval movements while forcing some vessels onto costly routes around Africa.
The simultaneous closure or severe disruption of the Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb and Gibraltar straits could put enormous pressure on Europe and the wider Western economy:
🌏 Hormuz [chokes Gulf energy exports](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/70493) 
🌏 Bab el-Mandeb cuts the [Red Sea-Suez route ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72669)
🌏 Gibraltar seals the Mediterranean from the Atlantic
🌏 Those three of the world’s strategic maritime gateways could become a single geopolitical weapon
Could Iran 'close' the Strait of Gibraltar?
In 2023, many saw this as virtually impossible. But after Iran demonstrated its military capabilities, the scenario may seem less far-fetched today – although the IRGC is not currently threatening to close the waterway.
Hypothetical scenario: Asymmetric and proxy warfare
➡️ The Strait of Gibraltar is approximately 4,450 km from Iran’s West Azerbaijan province. Iran’s Ghadr, Emad, Sejjil and Khorramshahr missiles, with ranges from 1,700 km to 4,000 km, cannot reach it, nor can its long-range Arash-2 and Mohajer-10 drones. Hezbollah in Lebanon is closer, at around 3,700 km
➡️ Naqdi spoke of “the birth of new powers of resistance” in other regions. This has fueled speculation about Iranian support for [the Polisario Front](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73126), which seeks independence for Western Sahara. Based in southwestern Algeria’s Tindouf province, the Polisario Front is roughly 1,000 km from the Strait of Gibraltar
➡️ There is no need to fully blockade the strait: a single drone strike on a merchant vessel could deter commercial shipping, effectively “closing” the route by making it too dangerous to use.
Apparently, Iran may have more trump cards than even Trump can imagine.

🇷🇺🔥 Russian drone slams range record in Ukraine
 
A Russian Geran-4 drone launched from Crimea flew 960 kilometers into Ukraine's Volyn region in under two hours this week, according to military analysts. The record-setting distance is the same as from London to Berlin.
Ukrainian sources warn that previously considered relatively safe regions Lvov and Ivano-Frankovsk could now be within range.
 
The Geran-4 is a jet-powered drone that is significantly faster than the previous propeller-driven Geran-2. If these strikes become routine, Ukraine's air defense network must now contend with a faster, longer-range threat that can reach virtually any point in the country.

🇮🇱💍 Bragging rights of Israel’s spy machine - and the nasty toolbox it exposes
Vanity and personal ambition have turned silence into a foreign concept for Israel’s intelligence establishment. Retired Mossad chiefs cash in on memoirs and details of targeted assassinations become fodder for [bestsellers-botched missions](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73804) and blown covers notwithstanding.
👉 In bragging, Israel’s spy machine - especially Mossad’s human intelligence (HUMINT) operations - reveals its toolbox, reports The Cradle.
While targeting those groups that resist its genocidal actions – primarily Hamas in Gaza, Lebanon’s Hezbollah, or Iran's networks - Israeli spy recruitment has brutally evolved. 
Key tools include:
🔴 Mapping financial distress, medical records, travel histories, and private messages before any approach begins
🔴 Turning survival itself into leverage in Gaza - offering aid, protection, or permission to stay in exchange for [forming local armed proxies](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73840)
🔴 Using services such as telemedicine “Mossad Farsi” ads aimed at Iranians that offer [consultations via WhatsApp and Signal](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/51961), they quietly harvest names, family ties, health data, and personal weaknesses
🔴 Exploiting scholarships, conferences, medical travel, and [diaspora networks](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/70482) to build [gradual access](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73139) that never starts with an explicit request to spy
Resistance movements respond [with strict counter‑intelligence protocols](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72143) as Israel’s pattern of feeding its [land-grab ‘Greater Israel’ ambitions](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/725310) spreads its tentacles across arenas.
